title: The centre of a general connected group and affineness with zero-dimensional centre
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Group schemes and homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], closed and normal subgroups as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme], and finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Affine means isomorphic to the spectrum of a commutative ring [def-pc-scheme]. Dimensions are topological Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected separated finite-type $k$-group scheme. The subfunctor assigning to a commutative $k$-algebra $B$ the elements of $G(B)$ commuting with every element of $G(B^{\prime})$ after every commutative $B$-algebra extension $B\to B^{\prime}$ is represented by a closed commutative normal subgroup scheme $Z\hookrightarrow G$. Write $Z^0$ for the connected component containing the identity, with its open-subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion]. Put $A=(Z^0)_{\mathrm{red}}$, the closed subscheme obtained by quotienting its structure sheaf by the nilradical [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Then $\dim A=\dim Z$. If $\dim Z=0$, then $G$ is affine. No affineness or commutativity assumption is imposed on $G$, and $Z$ need not be smooth.

source.place: Proposition 1.92 and following definition of the centre, printed pp.33--34; Corollary 1.35 and Proposition 1.38, printed pp.17--18 (components and reduction preserve dimension); Corollary 8.10, Corollary 8.11, printed pp.150--151, and Proposition 8.1(a), printed p.149. The zero-dimensional-centre implication is the first case of the proof of Theorem 8.26, printed p.154. No Stacks tag states this non-affine algebraic-group centre assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-fixed-point-action-finite-jets] to $H=G$, $X=G$, $x=e$, and the conjugation action $a(g,y)=gyg^{-1}$. The group axioms show that this is an action fixing $e$, and all its geometric hypotheses are exactly those on $G$. Choose $n\geq n_0$ and set $Z=\ker\rho_n$, a closed normal finite-type subgroup scheme supplied by the cited lemma. For every $B$, its points are precisely the $g\in G(B)$ satisfying $g_{B'}yg_{B'}^{-1}=y$ for all $B'$ and all $y\in G(B')$, equivalently commuting with all such $y$. This represents the required subfunctor on arbitrary, possibly nonreduced, test algebras. For $z,z'\in Z(B)$ take $B'=B$ and $y=z'$ to get $zz'=z'z$. Thus $Z$ is commutative as well as normal, by the functor-of-points definition [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup, def-sc-group-scheme].

source.place: Proposition 1.92 and centre definition, printed pp.33--34; Corollary 8.10, printed p.150.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-group-neutral-component-translates] to the finite-type group $Z$. Its identity component $Z^0$ is open and closed, and its finitely many connected components are translates isomorphic to $Z^0$. In a finite disjoint union of open-and-closed subsets every nonempty irreducible closed subset lies in one component: otherwise its intersections with one component and its complement decompose it into two proper closed subsets. A strictly increasing chain therefore lies in one component, so [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] gives $\dim Z=\dim Z^0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism], $A=(Z^0)_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $Z^0$ have homeomorphic underlying spaces. Homeomorphisms biject irreducible closed chains, hence $\dim A=\dim Z^0=\dim Z$.

source.place: Corollary 1.35 and following dimension discussion, printed p.17; reduction leaves the underlying space unchanged, as in Proposition 1.38, printed p.18.

proof.text: Assume $\dim Z=0$. The dimension comparison [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] identifies this topological dimension with the local-ring dimension used in [lem-pc-algebraic-dim-zero-affine-finite]. Apply the latter to the finite-type scheme $Z$ to obtain its affineness (indeed finiteness); properness and smoothness of $Z$ are not required. Factor the representation $\rho_n:G\to\operatorname{GL}(V_n)$ by [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] as $G\xrightarrow{q}I\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}(V_n)$, with $q$ faithfully flat and with the same kernel $Z$. Both source and target are separated finite-type group schemes: for the target, a basis identifies it with the spectrum of the finitely generated determinant localization in [def-sc-general-linear-group]. In particular the target is affine. By the affine description of a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], its closed subgroup $I$ is the spectrum of a quotient of that coordinate ring, and hence is affine.

source.place: Theorem 8.26 first case, printed p.154; Corollary 8.10, p.150; Theorem 5.39, p.108; Stacks Tag 06LH (varieties.tex, lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0).

proof.text: The homomorphism factorization gives the exact sequence $1\to Z\to G\xrightarrow{q}I\to1$ with $q$ flat and surjective and $Z$ its scheme-theoretic kernel. Both $Z$ and $I$ are affine by step 3. The affine-extension clause of [lem-sfb-exact-algebraic-group-property-permanence] now gives that $G$ is affine. This implication uses no reduction of the kernel, so it also covers a finite non-smooth centre.

source.place: Proposition 8.1(a), printed p.149, applied exactly as in Theorem 8.26 first case, printed p.154.

split_report.summary: Preserved the statement. Constructed the general centre as the stable kernel of finite-jet conjugation using one new action lemma, avoiding the existing affine-only conjugation lemma. Wrote the dimension comparison by component translations and reduction homeomorphism, and assembled the zero-dimensional-centre case from the existing dimension-zero, homomorphism-factorization and affine-extension nodes. Read Milne and every cited statement; no project attachment or Mathlib match states the item.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NE-187adc8de (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read Milne iAG2017 Thm 7.1 (pp.138-139), Prop 8.1 (p.149), Prop 8.9, Cor 8.10 and Cor 8.11 (pp.150-151), the Thm 8.26 first case (p.154), and the erratum that Prop 8.9 needs X reduced. New node lem-sfb-fixed-point-action-finite-jets states the intermediate claim of Milne 8.9: the jet kernels K_n descend and stabilise at N; then 7.1 and Krull show X^N=X. Assuming X smooth and connected gives integrality, which takes care of the erratum. H is not assumed affine. The statement is true on arbitrary B-points. Tested on the trivial action, X a point, G_m scaling A^1, and mu_p on A^1 in char p. It has no proof (B1), searches of all three kinds are recorded, and it is not a duplicate: the conjugation-finite-jet-kernel, dense- and torus-fixed-jet and adjoint-kernel nodes all assume affineness, which would be circular here. It does not restate the item. Item step 1: conjugation on G with fixed point e; the kernel is the centre functor, commutative by taking y=z'. Step 2: component translates plus the reduction homeomorphism give dim A=dim Z^0=dim Z. Step 3: the local-ring dimension bridge and the dim-0 finite-type lemma (not the proper variant) make Z affine; the factorization through a closed I in the affine GL(V_n) makes I affine. Step 4: the exact sequence and the affine clause of the property-permanence node (Milne 8.1(a)) make G affine. Hypotheses checked at each step; edge cases are trivial G, an elliptic curve and SL_p with centre mu_p. Accepted tool_uses: reduction-universal-homeomorphism, scheme-dimension-local-rings and algebraic-dim-zero-affine-finite, all generic. Batch-5: lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change and lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent are generic Mathlib-leaf facts (fppf base change, fpqc descent of smoothness). Neither is part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality statements or proofs, so both are accepted. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_centre_reducedIdentityComponent_dim_and_isAffine {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) [Smooth G.X.hom] [ConnectedSpace G.X.left] [IsSeparated G.X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.X.hom] [QuasiCompact G.X.hom] : ∃ (Z : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (i : Z ⟶ G) (Z0 : Z.X.left.Opens), IsClosedSubgroupScheme i.hom.hom ∧ IsNormalSubgroupScheme i.hom.hom ∧ IsCommMonObj Z.X ∧ (∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B], ReductiveTorusCentralizer.centralizerPoints (𝟙 G) B = Set.range (fun z : StandardGroupSchemes.affine k B ⟶ Z.X ↦ z ≫ i.hom.hom)) ∧ (Z0 : Set Z.X.left) = connectedComponent (GrpObj.onePoint Z.X) ∧ topologicalKrullDim Z0.toScheme.nilradical.subscheme = topologicalKrullDim Z.X.left ∧ (topologicalKrullDim Z.X.left = 0 → IsAffine G.X.left)

reviewed_lean.note: Statement matches the node clause by clause.
